events.location: Visitors staying with family or friends around the region
events.whosComing: Holiday visitors staying with family: families visiting relatives for Thanksgiving, with kids out of school; likely many repeat visitors, since they come to see family who live here.
events.notes: About 322 expected through the sheds from this listing today (2 parts below). • Staying with family or friends in the metro: about 1,100 of the roughly 16,200 people visiting relatives here for Thanksgiving come to the Quarter today, and about 1 in 5 of those pass through the sheds: about 216. Hotels can't see these visitors, so they aren't in the Free-range tourists listing (which counts only rentals, not friends and family, on these days). Market estimate: AAA's 81.8 million Thanksgiving travelers (Tue–Mon, 2025; the 2026 forecast wasn't out on Nov 9) × metro New Orleans's 0.37% of the U.S. population × about half staying with family or friends × about 2½ nights = about 54,000 a day in the metro over the week (more on Thanksgiving and the two days after); about 1 in 15 visit the Quarter on a given day and 1 in 5 of those pass through the sheds (an estimate; smaller than the Christmas holidays, as Thanksgiving trips are shorter). • Staying with family nearby (Baton Rouge, the Mississippi coast, Houma–Thibodaux, Hammond): about 420 of the roughly 21,100 holiday visitors staying with relatives within about 90 minutes come into the Quarter today (about 1 in 50 a day), and about 1 in 4 of those pass through the sheds: about 106. Market estimate: the same AAA method for those metro areas (about 0.48% of the U.S. population); a day trip into the Quarter at about a third of the metro's rate, with 1 in 4 of those who come passing through the sheds, as for a one-day visit.

events.title: Locals and regional visitors
events.location: Residents of the metro area and day-trippers from the region
events.whosComing: Locals and regional visitors: metro residents and regional day-trippers; families with kids on weekends and school holidays. The metro's median household income is about $62,400, below the U.S. median of $81,600 (Census, 2024). Many locals and regional visitors have been to the market many times, so depending on the merchandise, they may be less likely to buy than tourists, for whom everything is new and who are shopping for gifts and souvenirs.
events.notes: About 708 today: a plain weekday. Market estimate: about a third of the market's visitors live within a few hours' drive. Those who stay a night are counted with the everyday visitors or their event; this listing counts the rest, apart from those already in an event listing.

events.title: School field trips
events.location: Museums and sights of the French Quarter
events.whosComing: School field trips: K–12 students from schools across southeast Louisiana and the Mississippi coast, in chaperoned groups (about 1 adult for every 10 students), mostly on Tuesday–Friday mornings and middays. Their spending power is likely much lower than most other visitors', especially in the younger grades: many may not be allowed to carry money, or to hold up their chaperoned group to stop and buy.
events.notes: About 68 expected through the sheds: about 157 K–12 students and chaperones on French Quarter field trips today (a standing estimate; schools don't publish their trips). Timing: mostly Tuesday–Friday mornings and middays (the state museums are closed Mondays, so Mondays count half); none on weekends, holidays or school breaks. Market estimate: about 37,000 students and chaperones take a French Quarter field trip in a year (about one per student over K–12 in southeast Louisiana, fewer from the Mississippi coast), 11% of them in November; by where their trips go (the French Market named 100%, the Old U.S. Mint 75%, a stop within two blocks 50%, Jackson Square to Frenchmen and the riverfront 35%, elsewhere in the Quarter 10%), about 43% pass through the sheds.

events.title: Sports: Bayou Classic visitors in town

events.whosComing: Bayou Classic: Southern and Grambling alumni, students and families: college students and young adults (the lowest income per person of any age group, BLS) alongside alumni of all ages. Many drive in from Baton Rouge (about 80 miles), Grambling (about 300 miles) and across Louisiana and nearby states. Mostly repeat visitors: the Classic has been played in New Orleans nearly every year since 1974.
events.notes: About 32 expected through the sheds from this listing today. • Bayou Classic visitors in town: about 750 of the weekend's overnight visitors (a quarter of the city calendar's 50,000 for the weekend count as staying downtown: many fans drive in for the day, and students and families on a budget stay in cheaper hotels farther out or with family) are in town and free the morning after the game; most drive home today, so half the usual rate (a travel day). Plus about 1,100 staying farther out (outside downtown or with family; the weekend's visitors not counted downtown, less the day-trippers): the farther-out rate, 1 in 20, halved by the CBD pull to 1 in 40 × ½, about 14. In all about 32.
